newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols sink as rates hold.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols sink as rates hold.

text.p: Volatilities sank and call buyers emerged in major U.S. stock index options Tuesday afternoon after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, traders said.
News that rates were unchanged turned the bond and stock markets around and drove them both sharply into positive territory.
In late trade, the Dow industrial average .DJI was up 81 points at 7,310, its high for the session, after being down as much as 76 points earlier.
The broader S&P 500 index .SPX was up about eight points at 841.61 and the S&P 100 .OEX gained 10.13 to 828.59.
"Everybody was rushing in to buy calls initially" after the announcement was released around 1315 CDT/1815 GMT, one options broker said.

At 1430 CDT/1930 GMT, put volume in both the SPX and OEX continued to lead call volume, but the spread had narrowed. OEX puts totaled 31,194 and OEX calls totaled 23,650. In the SPX, put volume topped call volume by 64,034 to 24,781.
One index options dealer said volatilities dropped notably as the market rallied after the FOMC news.

The Chicago Board Options Exchange's (CBOE) volatility index .VIX, which is priced off certain OEX options, was down 2.10 points, or nearly 9.0 percent, at 21.54, in late trading, after climbing to 24.34 earlier.
"They dropped the market this morning as people were playing different opinions," the dealer said. "But volatilities dropped quickly" when the market reversed course.
The options broker said despite the market's strong rebound, gains may not last long, especially if bond prices begin to erode.
"Bonds love news and what we have is uncertainty," he said, explaining that investors will now be scrutinizing all the economic data to determine whether the Fed will raise rates at its July meeting.
"I think people are going to be extra nervous," he said. "The highs (in the stock market) have been made until at least August."
The Dow closed at a record 7,333.55 on May 15. On the same day, the OEX closed at a record 828.40 and the SPX at 841.88.
